_regression.source: real map: Inashiro (scripted hamlet) as generated 2026-08-16 with the fork newly recorded but BEFORE hamletgen's OFFTAKE_LADDER gave the hamlet rows a canal-B offtake. The GM: the channel 'takes a diagonal turn toward the southeast' but never 'split[s] and go[es] both along the northeast side and along the western side'. build_comb carves paddy on both sides of the bunsuiguchi fork (canal B shapes the far margin as a supply thread), yet with offtakes_b=() the bc arm is never inked - ~255 ft of planted paddy west of the fork against 0 ft of drawn supply, while the east flank shows 994/995. Researched (research/water.md 'The head-race forks - supply commands both flanks'): a gravity canal commands only ground below it (Chinese canal doctrine), and Minuma-dai (1728, the Kishu-school exemplar) deliberately divides its head into TWO canals along the two elevated margins. The fix: every OFFTAKE_LADDER row draws canal B (one offtake at ~0.55), inking the second arm partway down its margin.
